Type alias for a callable that, given a filename, returns a Stream* to which a module’s binary can be written. The callable is expected to allocate/open and return an output stream for that specific filename.

Represents a named binding to an index with optional source Location. Used as mapped values in BindingHash to associate identifier strings with an Index in the WABT toolchain. Constructors allow creating a binding with just an index, or with both a Location and an index.

Provides utilities to find duplicate name bindings and to look up the Index associated with a name or a Var. Inherits from std::unordered_multimap<std::string, Binding>; do not delete via a pointer to the base container because it lacks a virtual destructor.

A small utility class in namespace wabt that manages writing ANSI color escape codes to a FILE stream. It can be constructed with a FILE* and an enabled flag, and provides methods to emit specific color codes (Default, Bold, NoBold, Black, Red, Green, Yellow, Blue, Magenta, Cyan, White) and to retrieve the corresponding code strings (conditionally or unconditionally). Internally tracks the target FILE and whether color output is enabled. Details of SupportsColor and WriteCode are declared here but defined elsewhere.

128-bit SIMD-like value container providing lane-based getters/setters for various element widths. Backed by 16 bytes and uses endian-aware memcpy for lane access. Useful for representing WebAssembly v128 values. Default constructible; provides equality, zero checks, and mutators.

Symbol binding attribute values (global, weak, local).
Kinds of external definitions/imports/exports in WASM: function, table, memory, global, tag. Includes sentinels for range computation.

Resource limit descriptor for tables/memories: initial and optional max counts, with flags for shared memory and 64-bit index space (memory64). Provides IndexType helper returning I32 or I64. Constructors set has_max when max is provided.

Strongly-typed enumeration describing kinds of AST nodes used by the decompiler stage (e.g., expression node, declaration, statement aggregation, flush markers). Details beyond the enumerant names are inferred from usage in this header.

AST node representation used by wabt’s decompiler to transform standard IR into a higher-level structure. It stores the node kind (ntype), an IR expression type (etype) when relevant, a pointer to the original IR Expr, child nodes, and a small tagged union of annotations for flushing variables, declarations, or branch label type. Copy is disabled; movable only.

Top-level decompiler AST builder/owner. Manages transformation from wabt IR (Expr/ExprList from included headers) into Node trees, tracking expression/value stacks, block scopes, variable declarations, and special handling for multivalue/void expressions. Begins/ends function and block scopes via ModuleContext. Contains nested helper struct Variable for variable bookkeeping.
Small helper POD within AST for tracking a variable’s defining block and whether it has been defined. Used as the mapped value type in vars_defined.

Helper record inside LoadStoreTracking that captures a single memory access at a given offset: the accessed byte size, the inferred value type, the alignment used, a sequential index within a detected layout, and whether all accesses observed at that offset are uniform (same size/type/alignment).

Per-variable aggregation of memory accesses used to infer either a contiguous struct-like layout or a uniform typed pointer. Holds all LSAccess entries keyed by byte offset, flags for whether a struct layout is viable, and tracking for a single consistent element type/alignment when no struct layout exists.

Top-level tracker that walks decompiler AST nodes to collect memory load/store patterns per base address (typically locals), infer struct-like layouts or typed-pointer semantics, and generate lightweight type and access annotations for decompiled output.

Unnamed enumeration that defines two integral constants controlling the minimum and maximum sizes of generated content-based identifiers for data segments. These are intended as configuration values for renaming heuristics.

Top-level visitor class for traversing WebAssembly expression trees in wabt. It drives iteration over Expr, ExprList, and Func while delegating per-node handling to a Delegate implementation. Maintains internal state stacks to manage nested constructs like blocks, loops, if branches, and try/catch. Construction requires a Delegate*. Ownership/lifetime of the delegate is not specified here.

Abstract interface used by ExprVisitor to handle each concrete expression kind. Users subclass this and implement the pure-virtual callbacks to receive traversal events. Lifetime is managed by the owner that passes it to ExprVisitor; destructor is virtual.

Concrete no-op implementation of ExprVisitor::Delegate. All callbacks return Result::Ok, allowing users to subclass and override only the callbacks they care about, or to use as a default that ignores all nodes.

objects.definition: class OptionParser;
objects.description: Forward-declared class in namespace wabt. Only an incomplete declaration is provided here; its interface and purpose are not defined in this header. It is referenced as a parameter type for Features::AddOptions, implying it encapsulates command-line option parsing for feature flags.

Configurable feature flags for WABT (WebAssembly Binary Toolkit). For each feature listed in wabt/feature.def, this class generates accessors, mutators, and a backing boolean field initialized to the feature’s default. Calling setters triggers UpdateDependencies() to maintain consistency among interdependent features. EnableAll() enables all features defined in the feature.def. AddOptions registers CLI options with an OptionParser to control these flags. Concrete feature names, flags, defaults, and help text come from wabt/feature.def and are not visible in this header.

Represents a control-flow label within WebAssembly IR, carrying its name, label kind, parameter types consumed by the block, and result types produced. Used on a label stack to track the context of blocks/loops/ifs.

Analysis and bookkeeping context for a WABT Module. Tracks current function and a stack of control-flow labels to query label arity, function parameter/result counts, and to manage entry/exit of blocks/functions.

Small POD nested inside ModuleContext that describes the operand arity of an expression: number of arguments consumed, number of results produced, and whether the expression is statically unreachable.
Discriminant for wabt::Var indicating whether it holds an index or a name. It is part of Var’s internal tagged representation.

Tagged reference used throughout the IR to identify variables by index or name, and optionally carry a type reference for type-indexed contexts. Constructors allow creation from index, name, or type. Methods query and mutate the variant state and convert to a Type when appropriate.

Class that locates and returns source code lines and their offsets from an underlying LexerSource. Caches line offset ranges and provides APIs to fetch a line string with a column offset and to map a line number to byte offsets. Constructor takes ownership of a LexerSource. Exact behaviors of Result, Location, Offset, OffsetRange, ColumnRange are defined elsewhere.
Nested POD struct used to return a line of source text along with the starting column offset of the returned slice. Intended to be filled by GetSourceLine.

Opaque byte-stream wrapper used by WABT’s lexer to read from an in-memory buffer. It maintains a current read offset and provides tell/seek, ranged reads into vectors, and linear fills into a destination buffer. Non-copyable; offers Clone() to duplicate a source (implementation details not shown here). Construction requires a pointer to immutable data and its size. Lifetime of the underlying data must outlive the LexerSource instance.
Strongly-typed enum identifying the kind of numeric literal being parsed: integer, decimal float, hexadecimal float, infinity, or NaN. Used to guide floating-point parsing behavior.

Stores a densely packed enum of valid opcodes and can encode invalid opcodes via a negated prefix/code pair. Provides static instances for each opcode (Name_Opcode). Inner Info holds metadata such as name, types, memory size, and encoding. Construction is via static FromCode helpers; default ctor exists for union usage. Destruction is trivial. Simple byte buffer holder with helpers to write its contents to a file or stdout. Owns a std::vector<uint8_t> named data.
Concrete Stream that writes into an owned OutputBuffer in memory. Supports move construction, optional logging, clearing, and exporting or releasing the underlying buffer.

Concrete Stream that writes to a FILE*. Can be constructed from a filename or existing FILE*, supports move semantics, flushing, and provides factories for stdout/stderr. Tracks an internal offset and whether it should fclose the handle.

Represents a parsed literal token with its LiteralType and original textual spelling. Storage is a lightweight view over the source text; lifetime of the underlying text must outlive the Literal's use.
Strongly-typed enumeration of all token kinds recognized by WABT's lexer. The concrete values are populated via wabt/token.def and grouped with First_*/Last_* sentinels for category checks.

Lexical token produced by the tokenizer. Holds source location and a discriminated union for token payloads: text (for string-like tokens), Type/RefKind, Opcode, or Literal. The active union member is indicated by token_type_. Note: std::string_view and Literal reference external storage; the referenced source buffer must outlive the Token.

Main class that performs WebAssembly type-checking for instructions, blocks, and expressions. It manages a stack of types and a stack of labels, validates opcodes under specified feature flags, and exposes On* hooks mirroring instruction semantics. Constructed with a Features set and an external map of function types it can consult/update.
Lightweight function type record used by TypeChecker. Holds parameter/result type vectors and an associated type index into a module-level type section.

Represents a control-flow label (block/loop/if/try) tracked during type checking. Stores parameter and result type signatures, stack limit at entry, reachability state, and per-local reference-set flags. Provides helper to select branch types depending on label kind.

objects.definition: using ErrorCallback = std::function<void(const char* msg)>;
objects.description: Callback type invoked by TypeChecker to report human-readable error messages. Accepts a C-string and returns void.

Primary WebAssembly value/reference type wrapper used throughout WABT. Encodes both primitive value types (i32, f32, etc.) and reference types (funcref/externref and typed refs with indices), plus utility pseudo-types (Any, Void). Provides helpers for nullability, reference kinds, and conversion to inline vectors. It stores an Enum code and, for reference types with indices or generic ref nullability, a type_index_. Construction constraints are enforced via asserts.

Enumeration of all WebAssembly value and reference type codes as used by WABT; values mirror the binary encoding (negative numbers) and include internal pseudo-types (Any, I8U/I16U/I32U). Declared as a nested enum within wabt::Type.
Auxiliary enum specifying nullability for non-typed references (funcref/externref). Used in wabt::Type to indicate whether a generic ref is nullable.

objects.definition: using TypeVector = std::vector<Type>;
objects.description: Alias for a vector of wabt::Type used to represent sequences of types (e.g., function params/results).

objects.definition: struct Module;
objects.description: Forward declaration of wabt::Module, representing a WebAssembly module in the WABT toolchain. Only a declaration is present here; the full definition is in another header/source file. Details such as fields and ownership semantics are unknown from this header.

objects.definition: struct Script;
objects.description: Forward declaration of wabt::Script, representing a WAST/WAT script that may contain multiple modules and commands. Only a declaration is present here; full definition is elsewhere. Specific structure and ownership are not available in this header.

A lexical scanner for WebAssembly text (WAST). It tokenizes an input provided via a LexerSource and produces Token objects. Provides helper methods to classify characters, read numbers/strings, and manage source locations. Owns a LexerSource and can create a LexerSourceLineFinder. Construction requires a LexerSource, filename, and error sink (Errors*). Copy and assignment are disabled.

Options controlling how the WAST parser behaves: which WebAssembly features are enabled, whether to emit debug parsing output, and whether to allow parsing of binary modules embedded in text. Constructible with a Features object. Ownership/lifetime is managed externally by callers of the parser; no special destruction required.

objects.definition: using TokenTypePair = std::array<TokenType, 2>;
objects.description: Type alias for a pair of token types representing a two-token lookahead in the lexer/parser pipeline.

Top-level parser for WAT/WAST text format. Consumes tokens from a WastLexer and produces Module or Script IR. Provides many helper parse routines and internal resolution structures for reference types. Instances are constructed with pointers to a lexer, error sink, and parse options; it does not own these pointers. Contains nested helper types (ConstType enum class, several resolver structs, and a TokenQueue class) used during parsing.

Options bag controlling how a WebAssembly module is written to WAT (text) format. Holds the selected feature set and booleans that toggle expression folding and whether exports/imports are written inline. Constructible with defaults or from a Features instance.

A descriptor type for a WebAssembly module used by the interpreter. Only referenced by pointer in this header; the definition is not included here.
Forward declaration of a Stream class in the wabt namespace. The full definition is not present in this header, so its members and ownership semantics are unknown.

Function declaration returning std::string; not a type definition. No custom data type is defined here. Note: Included only to clarify absence of a type; there is no new typedef or struct introduced by this declaration.
Owns and manages all allocated interpreter Objects, roots for GC, features, and active Threads. Provides allocation, type-safe lookup, and garbage collection support.
Abstract GC-managed base class for all runtime entities (modules, instances, functions, tables, etc.). Tracks kind, GC mark, self reference, and host metadata/finalizer.
Runtime error object carrying a message and stack trace. Used to signal traps from execution.
Runtime handle for a passive/active data segment. Wraps a DataDesc from the module and tracks remaining size; supports range checks and drop.
Runtime handle for an element segment, materialized as a vector of refs. Supports range checks, dropping, and GC marking.
GC-managed compiled module containing canonicalized descriptors and import/export type lists.
A live instantiation of a Module: owns vectors of exported object Refs and live element/data segments. Provides instantiation helper and GC marking.
Execution context with value/call stacks and helpers to run or step instructions. Integrates with Store for GC and resource lookup. Thread::Options configures stack sizes and tracing.
Opaque host-owned payload wrapper to attach arbitrary native pointer with lifetime managed by GC. Useful for embedding host resources.
Thrown value carrying a tag reference and argument payloads for exception handling support.
Abstract base for importable/exportable externs (funcs, tables, memories, globals, tags). Provides type matching API against ImportType.
Base class for callable functions (defined and host). Holds FuncType and implements common call plumbing.
Interpreter-owned function backed by module code (Istream). Knows its Instance and FuncDesc for locals/handlers/code offset.
Function implemented by host callback with a declared FuncType. Executed via provided std::function.
Reference table storing Refs with a declared TableType. Supports growth, init/fill/copy, and GC traversal.
Linear memory buffer with wasm page-based growth. Implements loads/stores, inits, copies, and (fake) atomics with range checking.
Mutable or immutable global variable with a declared GlobalType. Provides typed get/set and host reference assignment.
Exception tag type object used to create and match exceptions. Non-callable extern.
Activation record for a call frame in the interpreter: stores function ref, stack heights, return/current offset, and cached instance/module.
Opaque handle referencing an Object in the Store via index. RefVec is a vector of such handles.
Generic fixed-lane SIMD vector with endian-safe indexing. Aliases provide concrete lane types and widths for wasm SIMD operations.
Type descriptor base for importable/exportable externs. Carries ExternKind and supports cloning.
Function signature: parameter and result value types and optional pointer to canonical func type table for reference equality checks.
Table extern type describing element reference type and min/max limits.
Linear memory type with limits and page size (bytes per page).
Global variable type specifying value type and mutability.
Exception tag type with attributes and payload signature (value types of exception arguments).
Describes a single import by module and name with its expected ExternType. Copyable; owns a clone of the type.
Describes a single export by name and its ExternType. Copyable; owns type clone.
Module field wrapping an ImportType; used in ModuleDesc for structural clarity.
Describes local variables of a function: repeated type count and cumulative end index for binary search mapping from local index to type.
Metadata for a single catch handler: tag index, handler offset, and whether it uses reference catch-all.
Describes exception handling region for a try/catch or try/delegate, with catch entries or delegate target, stack heights to restore, and bounds.
Static description of a function body: signature, locals layout, code start in Istream, and exception handlers.
Module-level table description with its type and initializer function (for active segments).
Module-level memory description with its type.
Module-level global description with type and initializer expression compiled into a FuncDesc.
Module-level tag description containing its TagType.
Module-level export entry associating an ExportType with the exported index into the appropriate kind's space.
Represents a start function index for module initialization.
Module-level data segment description including raw bytes, segment mode, target memory index, and initializer expression.
Module-level element segment description: elements (as init funcs), element ref type, mode, target table index, and initializer.
Complete static description of a module as compiled by WABT: types, imports, definitions, segments, exports, start functions, and the instruction stream.
Tagged storage for wasm values with helpers to construct/get/set primitive, vector, and reference types. TypedValue pairs a type tag with a value.
Alias of ExternalKind from wabt; only referenced, not defined here. Skipped details per instructions.

objects.definition:
enum class InstrKind {
  Imm_0_Op_0,                  // Nop
  Imm_0_Op_1,                  // i32.eqz
  Imm_0_Op_2,                  // i32.add
  Imm_0_Op_3,                  // select
  Imm_Jump_Op_0,               // br
  Imm_Jump_Op_1,               // br_if
  Imm_Index_Op_0,              // global.get
  Imm_Index_Op_1,              // global.set
  Imm_Index_Op_2,              // table.set
  Imm_Index_Op_3,              // memory.fill
  Imm_Index_Op_N,              // call
  Imm_Index_Index_Op_3,        // memory.init
  Imm_Index_Index_Op_N,        // call_indirect
  Imm_Index_Offset_Op_1,       // i32.load
  Imm_Index_Offset_Op_2,       // i32.store
  Imm_Index_Offset_Op_3,       // i32.atomic.rmw.cmpxchg
  Imm_Index_Offset_Lane_Op_2,  // v128.load8_lane
  Imm_I32_Op_0,                // i32.const
  Imm_I64_Op_0,                // i64.const
  Imm_F32_Op_0,                // f32.const
  Imm_F64_Op_0,                // f64.const
  Imm_I32_I32_Op_0,            // drop_keep
  Imm_I8_Op_1,                 // i32x4.extract_lane
  Imm_I8_Op_2,                 // i32x4.replace_lane
  Imm_V128_Op_0,               // v128.const
  Imm_V128_Op_2,               // i8x16.shuffle
};
objects.description: Enumeration grouping instruction formats by the shape of their immediates and operand counts to simplify decoding, disassembly, and tracing.
Decoded instruction holding the opcode, its categorized kind, and a union of immediate payload encodings used by various instruction forms.
Instruction stream builder/reader for the interpreter. Supports emitting serialized instructions with immediates, resolving fixups, reading back decoded Instrs, and disassembling/tracing.
Abstract interface used by Istream tracing/disassembly to supply per-instruction header text and to pick which instruction to display/select. Implementers provide contextual strings.
Concrete TraceSource used for disassembly output; overrides header and instruction selection formatting for disassembler use.

functions.name: wabt::Clz
functions.description: Counts the number of leading zero bits in the binary representation of x. If x is 0, returns the bit-width of unsigned (typically 32). Intended for bit-twiddling and fast log2-like operations.
requirements: x is an unsigned value; all values are accepted, including 0 (returns bit-width).
Return is an int in the range [0, sizeof(unsigned)*8].
No side effects; pure computation.

functions.name: wabt::Ctz
functions.description: Counts the number of trailing zero bits in the binary representation of x. If x is 0, returns the bit-width of unsigned (typically 32). Useful for isolating least-significant set bit position.
requirements: x is an unsigned value; all values are accepted, including 0 (returns bit-width).
Return is an int in the range [0, sizeof(unsigned)*8].

functions.name: wabt::Popcount
functions.description: Counts the number of one bits (population count) in an 8-bit integer.
requirements: x is an 8-bit unsigned value; all values are accepted.
Return is an int in the range [0, 8].

functions.name: wabt_snprintf
functions.signature: int wabt_snprintf(char* str, size_t size, const char* format, ...)
functions.description: Wrapper/macro alias for snprintf. Formats and writes output to the buffer str, writing at most size bytes including the terminating null, and returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding the null). In this configuration it is defined as a macro to snprintf.
requirements: str may be null only if size is 0; otherwise must be a valid, writable buffer of at least size bytes.
size can be 0 (no characters written, but return value still the number that would have been written).
format must be a valid format string; variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
The function returns a non-negative value on success; if the output is truncated, the return value exceeds or equals size; negative return indicates encoding or other errors on some platforms.

functions.name: wabt_vsnprintf
functions.signature: int wabt_vsnprintf(char* str, size_t size, const char* format, va_list ap)
functions.description: Wrapper/macro alias for vsnprintf. Formats and writes output to str using a va_list. In this configuration it is defined as a macro to vsnprintf.
requirements: str may be null only if size is 0; otherwise must be a valid, writable buffer of at least size bytes.
size can be 0 (no characters written, but return value still the number that would have been written).
format must be a valid format string; ap must be an initialized va_list corresponding to the format.
The function returns a non-negative value on success; if the output is truncated, the return value exceeds or equals size; negative return indicates encoding or other errors on some platforms.

functions.name: wabt_convert_uint64_to_double
functions.description: Converts an unsigned 64-bit integer to a double-precision floating-point value. Intended to ensure consistent conversion semantics across platforms.
requirements: x is any uint64_t value; all values are accepted.
Callers should be aware that not all uint64_t values are exactly representable in double (precision is ~53 bits); large values may lose precision.

functions.name: wabt_convert_uint64_to_float
functions.description: Converts an unsigned 64-bit integer to a single-precision floating-point value.
requirements: x is any uint64_t value; all values are accepted.
Many uint64_t values are not exactly representable in float (precision is ~24 bits); large values may overflow to infinity.

functions.name: wabt_convert_int64_to_double
functions.description: Converts a signed 64-bit integer to a double-precision floating-point value.
requirements: x is any int64_t value; all values are accepted.
Very large magnitude integers may not be exactly representable (precision is ~53 bits).

functions.name: wabt_convert_int64_to_float
functions.description: Converts a signed 64-bit integer to a single-precision floating-point value.
requirements: x is any int64_t value; all values are accepted.
Large magnitude integers may overflow to infinity or lose precision (float precision is ~24 bits).

functions.name: wabt::ApplyNames
functions.description: ApplyNames walks the given WABT IR module and replaces numeric variable references (e.g., function indices, import indices, function type indices, parameter and local indices) with their corresponding symbolic names wherever available. This mutates the module in place so later printing/processing uses names like $foo instead of raw indices. Typical usage is after parsing/reading a module and before emitting text or performing name-aware analyses. Returns a Result indicating success or failure.
requirements: module must be a valid, initialized wabt::Module representing a parsed WebAssembly module.
module must not be null.
The function mutates the provided module in place; callers should not assume the module remains byte-for-byte identical after the call.
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result and handle failure appropriately (e.g., do not proceed assuming names were applied if the result indicates an error).

functions.name: wabt::ReadBinaryIr
functions.description: Parses a WebAssembly binary module from the given memory buffer into a wabt::Module (IR). Intended for clients that have a WASM binary blob in memory and want a populated IR module while collecting any parsing/validation errors. The filename is used for diagnostics (e.g., error messages) and may not affect parsing. Returns a wabt::Result indicating success or failure. Details about error reporting or exact option effects are not documented here and are inferred from typical WABT usage.
requirements: The memory region [data, data + size) must be valid and readable for the duration of the call.
size must be the exact number of bytes available at data that constitute the WebAssembly binary to read.
out_module must be a valid, non-null pointer to a wabt::Module that can be populated by this function.
options must reference a valid, initialized wabt::ReadBinaryOptions object for the duration of the call.
The caller should provide a valid Errors* (unknown if null is allowed); if non-null it will receive any diagnostics produced during reading.
filename should point to a null-terminated string used for diagnostics (unknown if null is permitted).
The function’s return value (wabt::Result) must be checked by the caller to detect parsing/validation failure.
The caller retains ownership of the data buffer and is responsible for its lifetime management; it must outlive the call.

functions.name: wabt::BinaryReaderLogging::OnError
functions.description: Callback invoked on parse/read error to log the error and decide whether to continue. Returns true to continue, false to stop (typical delegate contract).
requirements: The Error reference must refer to a valid error object for the duration of the call.
Return value semantics beyond typical delegate usage are unknown; consult implementation for precise policy.

functions.name: wabt::ReadBinary
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::ReadBinary(const void* data, size_t size, wabt::BinaryReaderDelegate* reader, const wabt::ReadBinaryOptions& options);
functions.description: Parses a WebAssembly binary module from the given buffer and dispatches parse events to the provided BinaryReaderDelegate according to the options.
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
reader must be a valid, non-null delegate instance for the duration of the call.
If options.log_stream is provided, it must remain valid during parsing.
If options.skip_function_bodies is true, function bodies may be skipped (behavior depends on implementation).
The buffer should contain a valid wasm binary; otherwise OnError may be invoked and the Result may indicate failure.

functions.name: wabt::ReadU32Leb128
functions.signature: size_t wabt::ReadU32Leb128(const uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end, uint32_t* out_value);
functions.description: Reads an unsigned 32-bit LEB128 value from [ptr, end), writing the decoded value to out_value and returning the number of bytes consumed.
requirements: ptr must be <= end; the buffer between ptr and end must contain a valid unsigned LEB128-encoded value that fits in 32 bits.
out_value must be non-null and writable.
The function does not advance ptr; callers must add the returned byte count to advance.

functions.name: wabt::ReadI32Leb128
functions.signature: size_t wabt::ReadI32Leb128(const uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end, uint32_t* out_value);
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit LEB128 value (signed per name; actual sign handling unspecified here due to header type) from [ptr, end), writing the decoded value to out_value and returning the number of bytes consumed. Details on signedness are unknown due to the uint32_t out parameter type in the declaration.
requirements: ptr must be <= end; the buffer must contain a valid LEB128-encoded 32-bit value.
out_value must be non-null and writable.
The function does not advance ptr; callers must add the returned byte count to advance.

functions.name: wabt::WriteBinarySpecScript
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::WriteBinarySpecScript(wabt::Stream* json_stream, wabt::WriteBinarySpecStreamFactory module_stream_factory, wabt::Script* script, std::string_view source_filename, std::string_view module_filename_noext, const wabt::WriteBinaryOptions& options)
functions.description: Writes a WebAssembly spec script to a JSON stream while emitting each referenced module to a binary stream produced by the provided factory. Use this overload when you want to control how/where each module binary is written (e.g., to files or custom streams). Returns a wabt::Result indicating success or failure. Notes: module_stream_factory is invoked with the target module filename (no extension applied beyond what the implementation uses) and must return a writable wabt::Stream* for the module; json_stream receives the spec JSON describing the script and module references.
requirements: json_stream must be a valid, writable wabt::Stream pointer (non-null).
module_stream_factory must be a valid callable; it will be called with a filename and must synchronously return a non-null wabt::Stream* suitable for writing binary data.
script must be a valid wabt::Script pointer (non-null and initialized with the script to serialize).
source_filename should identify the original script source; content is used for metadata; must outlive the call.
module_filename_noext is the base name used when generating module output filenames; must outlive the call.
options must reference a valid wabt::WriteBinaryOptions instance whose lifetime covers the call.
Caller must check the returned wabt::Result for success/failure and handle errors accordingly.

Any streams returned by module_stream_factory must remain valid for the duration of the call; ownership/lifetime management beyond the call is implementation-dependent and not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: wabt::WriteBinaryModule
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::WriteBinaryModule(wabt::Stream* stream, const wabt::Module* module, const wabt::WriteBinaryOptions& options)
functions.description: Serialize a WebAssembly Module into the binary format and write it to the provided Stream. Typical usage is to emit a compiled/translated module to a file or memory-backed stream using the specified WriteBinaryOptions (features, canonicalization, relocatable output, and debug names). Returns a Result indicating success or failure.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized wabt::Stream* capable of accepting writes; must not be null.
module must be a valid, fully-initialized wabt::Module* describing the module to serialize; must not be null.
options must be a valid reference to a configured wabt::WriteBinaryOptions struct; features should match what the module requires.
Caller must check the returned wabt::Result and handle failure.

functions.name: wabt::WriteType
functions.signature: void wabt::WriteType(wabt::Stream* stream, wabt::Type type, const char* desc = nullptr)
functions.description: Write a single wasm Type value to the stream, optionally including a textual description label for diagnostic or annotation purposes. Useful when emitting sections that encode value types or signatures.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized wabt::Stream*; must not be null.
type should be a valid wabt::Type value.
desc may be nullptr or a pointer to a null-terminated C string describing the value being written.

functions.name: wabt::WriteStr
functions.signature: void wabt::WriteStr(wabt::Stream* stream, std::string_view s, const char* desc, wabt::PrintChars print_chars = wabt::PrintChars::No)
functions.description: Write a length-prefixed string (or otherwise appropriately encoded string for wasm) to the stream with an associated description label. The print_chars flag controls whether character data is emitted/escaped for diagnostics when supported.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized wabt::Stream*; must not be null.

functions.name: wabt::MemcpyEndianAware
functions.signature: void wabt::MemcpyEndianAware(void* dst, const void* src, size_t dsize, size_t ssize, size_t doff, size_t soff, size_t len)
functions.description: Copies len bytes from src+soff to dst+doff, accounting for target endianness (on big-endian builds, adjusts offsets from the end of the buffers; on little-endian, copies directly). Use to move subranges between differently-sized or endian-sensitive buffers.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of size at least dsize bytes.
src must point to a readable buffer of size at least ssize bytes.
doff+len must be <= dsize; soff+len must be <= ssize.
Behavior depends on compile-time endianness (WABT_BIG_ENDIAN).
Buffers may overlap only as permitted by memcpy (no guarantee for overlapping regions).

requirements: sizeof(T) must be <= 16 (compile-time).
(lane + 1) * sizeof(T) must be <= 16.

requirements: sizeof(T) must be <= 16 (compile-time).
(lane + 1) * sizeof(T) must be <= 16.

requirements: sizeof(Src) must equal sizeof(Dst) (compile-time).

functions.name: wabt::AST::AST
functions.description: Constructs an AST builder bound to a ModuleContext and an optional function. If f is non-null, begins function processing (mc.BeginFunc), seeds the local variable name table for parameters, and arranges to end the function (mc.EndFunc) in the destructor.
requirements: mc must remain valid for the lifetime of this AST instance.
If f != nullptr, mc must be in a state where BeginFunc(*f) is legal; this constructor will call mc.BeginFunc(*f).
If f != nullptr, the destructor will call mc.EndFunc(); callers must not independently end the same function in mc while this AST is alive.
If f != nullptr, f->GetNumParams() must be valid and f must remain valid for the constructor’s execution.

functions.name: wabt::AST::~AST
functions.description: Destructor; if constructed with a non-null function pointer, it finalizes function processing by calling mc.EndFunc().

functions.name: wabt::AST::InsertNode
functions.signature: wabt::Node& wabt::AST::InsertNode(wabt::NodeType ntype, wabt::ExprType etype, const wabt::Expr* e, wabt::Index nargs)
functions.description: Creates a new AST node with the given type and associated IR Expr pointer, pops nargs existing nodes from the expression stack as its children, and pushes the new node back on the stack. Returns a reference to the inserted node (the one now on the top of the stack).
requirements: exp_stack.size() must be >= nargs; otherwise an assertion will fail.
nargs must match the number of child expressions intended to be attached to the node.
e may be null for synthesized nodes; if non-null it must point to a valid wabt::Expr that remains alive for the duration of AST construction.

functions.name: wabt::AST::PreDecl
functions.signature: template <wabt::ExprType T> void wabt::AST::PreDecl(const wabt::VarExpr<T>& ve)
functions.description: Function template that records a forward declaration for a variable (typically a local) if it has not already been predeclared. Intended to ensure a declaration exists when a variable is used before its first definition.
requirements: ve.var.name() must be a valid variable identifier in the current context.
Primarily intended to be used internally when detecting use-before-definition; it performs a linear search over predecls (note in comments it is slow).

functions.name: wabt::AST::Get
functions.signature: template <wabt::ExprType T> void wabt::AST::Get(const wabt::VarExpr<T>& ve, bool local)
functions.description: Function template that handles a variable read (get) of a local or global. Tracks variable definition scope for locals and inserts an expression node for the get operation.
requirements: If local == true, ve must reference a valid local; if local == false, ve must reference a valid global.
Updates internal vars_defined state for locals; callers should only pass local == true for locals to avoid incorrect lifting/predecl behavior.
Pushes a node with zero children; the internal expression/value stacks must be in a consistent state when calling.

functions.name: wabt::AST::Set
functions.signature: template <wabt::ExprType T> void wabt::AST::Set(const wabt::VarExpr<T>& ve, bool local)
functions.description: Function template that handles a variable write (set) of a local or global. For a first-time local assignment at top value-stack depth, it emits a DeclInit; otherwise it records a predeclaration if needed and emits an assignment expression node.
requirements: If local == true, ve must reference a valid local; if local == false, ve must reference a valid global.
Assumes there is exactly one value available on the expression/value stack to assign; it emits a node consuming 1 child.
May emit a declaration for first-use locals when the internal value_stack_depth indicates a top-level context.

functions.name: wabt::AST::Block
functions.signature: template <wabt::ExprType T> void wabt::AST::Block(const wabt::BlockExprBase<T>& be, wabt::LabelType label)
functions.description: Function template that constructs a structured block or loop AST node. Begins a labeled block in the ModuleContext, constructs the inner expressions using the block’s signature (params/results), ends the block, and pushes a node representing the block expression.
requirements: be.block must be a valid block structure with a decl containing accurate GetNumResults() and GetNumParams().
label must be an appropriate LabelType for the block kind (e.g., Block or Loop).
ModuleContext must accept a matching BeginBlock/EndBlock pair around the provided block.

functions.name: wabt::AST::Construct
functions.description: Constructs AST nodes for a single IR expression e. Dispatches on e.type() to handle gets/sets, control flow (if/block/loop/branches), and generic expressions using ModuleContext-provided arity. Updates internal expression/value stacks accordingly.
requirements: e must be a valid wabt::Expr for which mc.GetExprArity(e) is defined.
Relies on internal invariants of exp_stack and value stack depth; should be used within a well-formed construction sequence.

functions.name: wabt::Node::Node
functions.description: Default constructor; initializes a Node to Uninitialized node type, Nop expression type, null expression pointer, and empty children. Node-specific union fields are left zero-initialized.

functions.name: wabt::Node::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator; assigns from rhs by transferring its contents and resetting rhs to a moved-from state (ntype Uninitialized, etype Nop). Also swaps children vectors and copies the union.
requirements: rhs must be an rvalue Node.
After assignment, do not rely on rhs’s prior contents; it has been moved-from and partially reset.

functions.name: wabt::GetDecompTypeName
functions.description: Maps a wabt::Type enum value to a human-readable decompiler type name (e.g., I32 -> "int", I8U -> "ubyte"). Used to produce readable type names when emitting decompiled code. Returns "ILLEGAL" for unrecognized/unsupported types.
requirements: Input t must be a valid wabt::Type enumeration value; unknown values will yield the string "ILLEGAL".
The returned pointer refers to a static string literal and must not be freed or modified.

functions.name: wabt::GetMemoryType
functions.description: Derives the effective memory element type for a load/store based on the base operand type and the opcode. For integer loads/stores, inspects the opcode’s memory size and signedness suffix ("_u") to decide between signed/unsigned narrow/wide integer types (I8/I8U, I16/I16U, I32/I32U). Returns operand_type for non-integer cases or when no narrowing applies.
requirements: operand_type should be wabt::Type::I32 or wabt::Type::I64 for integer memory accesses to enable narrowing; otherwise operand_type is returned unchanged.
opc must represent a memory access opcode with a meaningful GetMemorySize() (1, 2, or 4) and GetName() consistent with WABT opcodes.
Behavior for SIMD and other non-integer types is currently not specialized (returns operand_type).

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::Track
functions.description: Traverses the expression tree rooted at n and records load/store accesses for later layout inference. It recurses over children and, for Load/Store nodes, calls LoadStore(...) with the computed parameters from the opcode and address expression.
requirements: n must be a valid AST node representing an expression subtree; its children vector must be well-formed.
For Load expressions, n.children[0] is expected to be the address expression; same for Store.
The AST node types and embedded expressions (LoadExpr/StoreExpr) must match n.etype (ExprType::Load/Store) as required by cast<>.
To use the collected information for struct layout decisions, call CheckLayouts() after finishing all Track() calls on a function.

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::AddrExpName
functions.description: Extracts an identifier name from an address expression node to associate memory accesses with a specific base variable. Currently recognizes local variable address expressions (LocalGet and LocalTee) and returns their variable name; returns an empty string for unsupported address forms.
requirements: addr_exp must be a valid AST node.
Only ExprType::LocalGet and ExprType::LocalTee are recognized; other expression types yield an empty string.
Returned string may be empty; callers must handle the empty case as "no identifiable base".

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::LoadStore
functions.signature: void wabt::LoadStoreTracking::LoadStore(uint64_t offset, wabt::Opcode opc, wabt::Type type, wabt::Address align, const wabt::Node& addr_exp)
functions.description: Records a single memory load/store access at the given offset relative to an identifiable base address expression. Normalizes the memory element type using GetMemoryType, checks alignment and uniformity across accesses, and aggregates per-base-variable access info for later layout/type inference.
requirements: addr_exp should be an address expression that AddrExpName can resolve to a non-empty base name (currently LocalGet or LocalTee); otherwise the access is ignored.
opc must describe a memory access with a meaningful GetMemorySize() and IsNaturallyAligned(align).
offset is the static memory offset of the access; it is used as the key within the base’s access map.
align should reflect the instruction’s alignment; non-natural alignment will mark the access as non-uniform (disabling struct layout for that base).
type is the instruction’s nominal result/param type; the effective memory type is derived via GetMemoryType(type, opc).

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::CheckLayouts
functions.description: Analyzes the collected accesses per base variable to determine if they form a regular, contiguous, and naturally aligned sequence usable as a struct layout. Marks each variable as struct_layout=true/false and assigns stable field indices for uniform, contiguous accesses; otherwise prefers pointer-to-single-type if applicable.
requirements: Call this after completing all Track()/LoadStore() calls for a function to finalize layout decisions before generating declarations or accesses.
Accesses with mixed sizes/types/alignments or non-natural alignment will disable struct layout for that variable.
If a variable has only one access, struct_layout is disabled to prefer pointer semantics.

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::IdxToName
functions.description: Converts a 0-based field index to a readable decompiler field name using IndexToAlphaName (e.g., 0->"a", 1->"b"). Used when emitting struct-like field names for inferred layouts.
requirements: idx must be a valid index previously assigned during CheckLayouts() for consistent naming.
Relies on the availability of wabt::IndexToAlphaName; behavior is unknown if that utility is altered.

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::GenAlign
functions.description: Generates an alignment suffix for a pointer type declaration. Returns an empty string for naturally aligned accesses; otherwise returns "@<align>" (e.g., "@2").
requirements: opc.IsNaturallyAligned(align) determines whether to emit an alignment suffix.
align must be the alignment used by the memory instruction and consistent with opc.

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::GenTypeDecl
functions.description: Produces a decompiler-style type declaration string for the tracked base variable named name. If its accesses form a struct layout, emits a fielded struct-like declaration (e.g., "{ a:int, b:float }"); otherwise, if all accesses share the same type/alignment, emits a typed pointer like "int_ptr@4". Returns an empty string if no meaningful declaration can be inferred or the name is unknown.
requirements: name must match a base variable recorded by previous Track()/LoadStore() calls; otherwise an empty string is returned.
For consistent struct emission, run CheckLayouts() before calling this method.
If struct_layout is false and same_type is Type::Void, no declaration is emitted (returns empty string).

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::GenAccess
functions.signature: std::string wabt::LoadStoreTracking::GenAccess(uint64_t offset, const wabt::Node& addr_exp) const
functions.description: Returns a field access string corresponding to a previously tracked memory access at the given offset for the given address expression. If a struct layout was inferred, returns the field name (e.g., "a"); if only a typed pointer was inferred, returns "*"; otherwise returns an empty string.
requirements: addr_exp must resolve via AddrExpName to a tracked base variable; otherwise an empty string is returned.
offset must correspond to a recorded access under that base; for struct layout, it must exist in the access map (asserts in debug builds).
Call CheckLayouts() beforehand to ensure struct field indices are assigned consistently.

functions.name: wabt::LoadStoreTracking::Clear
functions.description: Clears all tracked variables and their recorded accesses, resetting the tracking state for reuse on another function or analysis pass.
requirements: After Clear(), any subsequent GenTypeDecl/GenAccess calls will have no data until new Track()/LoadStore() calls are made.

functions.name: wabt::RenameToIdentifier
functions.signature: inline void wabt::RenameToIdentifier(std::string& name, Index i, BindingHash& bh, const std::set<std::string_view>* filter)
functions.description: Normalize an arbitrary string into a valid, unique identifier and update the binding map accordingly. The function filters non-identifier characters, collapses runs of underscores, trims parenthesized portions (e.g., C++ parameter lists), optionally removes specified snake_case words via the filter set, truncates overly long identifiers, and disambiguates by appending _N if needed. It removes the original binding for name from bh, then inserts the new identifier bound to Binding(i). Use when a single symbol’s name must be sanitized and made unique within a binding scope.
requirements: name must refer to the mutable name of the entity being renamed; it will be modified in place.
i must be the Index for the same entity represented by name; it will be stored in the new Binding inserted into bh.
bh must be the active BindingHash for the scope that currently may contain an entry for name; this function will erase the old key and emplace the new one.
filter may be null; if non-null, it must point to a valid std::set<std::string_view> for the duration of the call; words found between underscores are removed if present in the set.
The resulting identifier may be truncated to at most 100 characters and may be disambiguated by suffixing _<number>; callers must not assume the original name or length is preserved.
Not thread-safe for concurrent use on shared name or bh; external synchronization is required if used concurrently.

functions.name: wabt::RenameToIdentifiers
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
void wabt::RenameToIdentifiers(std::vector<T*>& things, BindingHash& bh, const std::set<std::string_view>* filter)
functions.description: Batch-rename a collection of entities to valid, unique identifiers by calling RenameToIdentifier on each element in order. Each T must expose a mutable std::string member named name. Uses the element index in the vector as the Binding Index when updating bh. Optionally filters out specified snake_case words using the provided filter set.
requirements: things must contain pointers to objects of type T; each pointer must be non-null and each T must have a publicly accessible std::string member named name.
The order of things determines the Index values passed to RenameToIdentifier (starting at 0 and incrementing by 1).
bh must be the binding map corresponding to this collection; it will be mutated to erase old keys and insert new ones for each renamed element.
filter may be null; if non-null, it must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Names of elements and bh will be modified; callers must not rely on previous names or bindings after the call.
Not thread-safe for concurrent mutation of things or bh without external synchronization.

functions.name: wabt::RenameToContents
functions.description: Assign content-derived identifiers to auto-generated data segment names. For segments whose current name begins with "d_", build a new identifier starting with "d_" and then appending alphanumeric/underscore characters found in the segment’s data, truncating at a maximum size. If the derived identifier is at least a minimum length and does not collide in bh, replace the segment’s name and update bh. Otherwise, keep the original name. Intended to produce more meaningful names for data segments.
requirements: segs must contain non-null DataSegment* elements; each DataSegment must expose name (std::string) and data (byte sequence) members.
Only segments with names starting with the literal prefix "d_" are considered for renaming; others are skipped.
The derived name length must be at least min_content_identifier_size (7) and is truncated at max_content_identifier_size (30). Names shorter than the minimum are not applied.
bh is mutated: if a rename occurs, the old key seg->name is erased and the new key is inserted with a Binding constructed from an index; callers must ensure bh corresponds to segs.
If the derived name already exists in bh, no rename occurs (the original generated name is kept).
Callers must not rely on previous segment names after this function, as some may change.
Not thread-safe for concurrent mutation of segs or bh without external synchronization.

functions.name: wabt::RenameAll
functions.description: Normalize and uniquify names across the entire module for decompiler output. Applies identifier filtering/normalization to functions (with a C++-oriented keyword filter), and to globals, tables, tags, exports, types, memories, data segments, and element segments (without keyword filtering). Then performs content-based renaming for data segments. Intended to be called after names have been populated from the binary (e.g., ReadBinaryIr and GenerateNames) and before names are propagated elsewhere (e.g., ApplyNames).
requirements: module must be a fully initialized wabt::Module with its vectors (funcs, globals, tables, tags, exports, types, memories, data_segments, elem_segments) and corresponding binding maps populated and consistent.
This function mutates module names and all related BindingHash maps; callers must not assume previous names or bindings persist.
Recommended call order (per comments): after ReadBinaryIr/GenerateNames have provided initial names, before ApplyNames further propagates names.
Not thread-safe for concurrent access to module without external synchronization.

functions.name: wabt::RenameAll
functions.description: Renames all applicable identifiers within a WebAssembly module in place. Typically used to assign stable, readable, or valid names (e.g., functions, globals, locals) across the module prior to emitting or decompiling it. Details of the renaming scheme are not documented here; behavior is inferred from the function name and location in the decompiler header.
requirements: module must refer to a valid, initialized wabt::Module that can be modified in place (non-const reference).
Callers should expect identifiers within the module to change after this call; any cached name-based lookups should be refreshed (inferred).
No error return is provided; failure modes are unknown from the header.

functions.name: wabt::Decompile
functions.signature: std::string wabt::Decompile(const wabt::Module& module, const wabt::DecompileOptions& options)
functions.description: Decompiles a WebAssembly module to a textual representation and returns it as a string. Likely produces a C-like or otherwise high-level decompiled form suitable for inspection; exact format and option effects are not documented here and are inferred from context.
requirements: module must be a valid, initialized wabt::Module representing the WebAssembly to decompile (const reference).
options must be a valid wabt::DecompileOptions instance; this header shows an empty struct, implying defaults only (unknown specifics).
The function returns the decompiled text as std::string; no separate error channel is exposed in the signature—failure handling is unknown from the header.

functions.name: wabt::FormatErrorsToString
functions.signature: std::string wabt::FormatErrorsToString(const Errors&, Location::Type, LexerSourceLineFinder* = nullptr, const Color& color = Color(nullptr, false), const std::string& header = {}, PrintHeader print_header = PrintHeader::Never, int source_line_max_length = 80);
functions.description: Formats a collection of wabt diagnostics into a single string. Intended for rendering Errors with optional source line lookups and optional ANSI colorization, with control over an optional header and maximum displayed source line length.
requirements: The Errors argument must refer to a valid, initialized collection of diagnostics (not a dangling reference).
Location::Type must correspond to the kind of locations contained in the Errors (e.g., file/offset type expected by the formatter).
If provided, LexerSourceLineFinder* must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized finder capable of mapping Locations to source lines; nullptr is allowed to omit source line lookups.
The Color object controls colorization; it must remain valid for the duration of the call. Passing Color(nullptr, false) disables color (default).
The header string is optional; printing behavior is controlled by print_header (Never, Once, Always).
source_line_max_length is a maximum length hint for rendered source lines; values should be non-negative; unusually large values may produce long output.

functions.name: wabt::FormatErrorsToFile
functions.signature: void wabt::FormatErrorsToFile(const Errors&, Location::Type, LexerSourceLineFinder* = nullptr, FILE* = stderr, const std::string& header = {}, PrintHeader print_header = PrintHeader::Never, int source_line_max_length = 80);
functions.description: Formats a collection of wabt diagnostics and writes them to a FILE* stream (stderr by default). Supports optional source line lookups, an optional header, and a maximum displayed source line length.
requirements: The Errors argument must refer to a valid, initialized collection of diagnostics (not a dangling reference).
Location::Type must correspond to the kind of locations contained in the Errors (e.g., file/offset type expected by the formatter).
If provided, LexerSourceLineFinder* must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized finder capable of mapping Locations to source lines; nullptr is allowed to omit source line lookups.
FILE* must be a valid, open C FILE stream suitable for writing; the default is stderr. Passing a null or closed stream results in undefined behavior.
The header string is optional; printing behavior is controlled by print_header (Never, Once, Always).
source_line_max_length is a maximum length hint for rendered source lines; values should be non-negative; unusually large values may produce long output.

functions.name: wabt::Features::AddOptions
functions.description: Registers feature-related command-line options with the provided OptionParser. Intended to be called during option/parser setup so that users can enable/disable individual WebAssembly features via flags.
requirements: The OptionParser* must point to a valid, initialized wabt::OptionParser instance.
Typically called before parsing command-line arguments so the options are recognized. Exact timing beyond setup is not specified.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not documented; assume calls should be serialized with other parser setup.

functions.name: wabt::Features::EnableAll
functions.description: Enables all known features by invoking the generated enable_<feature>() methods for every feature defined in wabt/feature.def. Use when you want all optional/experimental WebAssembly features turned on.
requirements: May be called at any time to set all feature flags to enabled; no parameters required.
Calling this updates internal dependencies via UpdateDependencies() as each feature is toggled.
Thread-safety is not documented; assume external synchronization if Features is shared.

functions.name: wabt::GetExtension
functions.description: Returns only the file extension (including the leading dot) from a filename or path string view. If no extension exists, returns an empty view. Typical usage is to inspect whether a given path ends with an extension like ".wasm" or ".wat" without allocating a new string.
requirements: filename may be any UTF-8/byte sequence; if it contains an extension, it will be returned with a leading '.'; otherwise an empty view is returned.
The returned std::string_view refers to the data underlying the input filename; the caller must ensure the input data remains valid for as long as the returned view is used.
No allocation or mutation occurs; the function is pure and does not throw under normal circumstances.

functions.name: wabt::StripExtension
functions.description: Returns the input path or filename with the final extension removed. If there is no extension, returns the original input. This does not modify directories—only the suffix after the last '.' is removed. The return is a view into the original input.
requirements: s may be any path or filename string; if it contains an extension, only the last extension component is removed.
The returned std::string_view refers to the data underlying the input s; the caller must ensure the input data remains valid for as long as the returned view is used.
Function is non-allocating and does not mutate inputs; behavior is deterministic for any input.

functions.name: wabt::GetBasename
functions.description: Returns the last path component (the basename) after the final slash in a path string view. If no slash is present, returns the input unchanged. Useful for extracting just the file name from a full path without allocation.
requirements: filename may be any path or filename string; the basename is determined by the last '/' character.
The returned std::string_view refers to the data underlying the input filename; the caller must ensure the input data remains valid for as long as the returned view is used.
No allocation or mutation occurs; the function is pure.

functions.name: wabt::GenerateNames
functions.signature: wabt::Result GenerateNames(wabt::Module* module, wabt::NameOpts opts = wabt::NameOpts::None);
functions.description: Generate readable names for unnamed entities in a WebAssembly module (e.g., functions, locals, etc.). The function operates in-place on the provided Module and returns a Result indicating success or failure. When the AlphaNames option is set, generated names use alphabetic sequences. Typical usage: call after loading/parsing a module to ensure all items have printable, stable names for debugging, tooling, or text format emission. Implementation details beyond this header are unknown; specifics of which entities are named and the exact naming scheme outside AlphaNames are inferred from identifiers.
requirements: module must be a valid, initialized wabt::Module pointer (must not be null).
opts must be a combination of wabt::NameOpts flags; recognized values in this header are NameOpts::None and NameOpts::AlphaNames.
The function mutates the provided module (callers should not assume const).
Callers should check the returned wabt::Result and handle non-success appropriately (exact error semantics unknown).

functions.name: wabt::IndexToAlphaName
functions.description: Convert a numeric index to a lowercase alphabetic name string using a base-26 scheme with letters 'a'..'z'. The least significant character comes first (e.g., 0 -> "a", 1 -> "b", 25 -> "z", 26 -> "ab"). Useful for generating compact, readable placeholder names. Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: index should be a non-negative wabt::Index value (type defined in wabt/common.h; typically an unsigned integer).
The function allocates and returns a new std::string; no special cleanup is required by the caller.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::GetLabelStackSize
functions.description: Returns the current number of labels on the internal label stack for this ModuleContext. Useful for validating structured control-flow scope depth during traversal or validation.
requirements: The ModuleContext instance must be initialized with a valid module (constructed).
No additional preconditions; callable at any time.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::GetLabel
functions.signature: const wabt::Label* wabt::ModuleContext::GetLabel(const wabt::Var& var) const
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to the Label corresponding to the given Var (label reference) in the current context. Typically used to resolve branch targets by name or depth while traversing/validating expressions. Returns a const Label*; behavior when the label is not found is not specified in this header (may be nullptr or may assert/throw in implementation).
requirements: There must be an active label scope such that var refers to an in-scope label on the current label stack.
var must identify a label by valid depth or name that exists in the current context.
Handling of non-existent labels is unknown; callers should be prepared for a null return or implementation-defined failure.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::GetLabelArity
functions.description: Returns the arity (number of values) associated with the specified label target. In WebAssembly validation, this is typically the number of result values expected when branching to that label.
requirements: There must be a label in scope matching var on the current label stack.
var must reference a valid label by name or depth.
Exact behavior for invalid var is unknown from this header; callers should avoid passing unresolved labels.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::SetTopLabelType
functions.description: Sets the LabelType of the label at the top of the label stack. Useful when the label’s type is determined after initial push (e.g., distinguishing block/loop/if).
requirements: The label stack must be non-empty; at least one BeginBlock (or equivalent) must have been called before this.
label_type must be a valid wabt::LabelType value.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::GetFuncParamCount
functions.description: Returns the number of parameter types for the function identified by var within the associated module. Supports function identification by index or name (per wabt::Var semantics).
requirements: The ModuleContext must reference a valid module containing the function identified by var.
var must resolve to an existing function; behavior for unresolved functions is not specified here.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::GetFuncResultCount
functions.description: Returns the number of result types for the function identified by var within the associated module.
requirements: The ModuleContext must reference a valid module containing the function identified by var.
var must resolve to an existing function; behavior for unresolved functions is not specified here.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::BeginBlock
functions.description: Begins a new structured control-flow block by pushing a corresponding Label onto the label stack, using the provided label_type and the block’s declared param/result types. Intended for use when entering block/loop/if constructs during traversal or validation.
requirements: Must be paired with a subsequent EndBlock to restore the label stack.
block must be a valid wabt::Block with coherent type annotations (param/result types) as expected by the implementation.
label_type must be a valid wabt::LabelType.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::EndBlock
functions.description: Ends the current structured control-flow block by popping the top label from the label stack. Intended to be called when leaving a block/loop/if construct.
requirements: There must be a previously begun block (i.e., label stack must be non-empty) before calling EndBlock.
BeginBlock/EndBlock calls should be properly nested and balanced.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::BeginFunc
functions.description: Marks the beginning of processing a function, setting the current function context and typically initializing the label stack for the function’s body (implementation-defined).
requirements: func must be a valid wabt::Func object from the associated module.
Should be paired with a corresponding EndFunc call after processing the function. Nesting multiple BeginFunc calls without an EndFunc is not supported.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::EndFunc
functions.description: Marks the end of processing the current function, clearing any state associated with the active function (e.g., current_func_ and any remaining labels, per implementation).
requirements: A corresponding BeginFunc must have been called previously; there must be an active function context.
Should only be called once per matching BeginFunc.

functions.name: wabt::ModuleContext::GetExprArity
functions.description: Computes the argument and result arities for the given expression in the current context, returning an Arities struct with nargs, nreturns, and an unreachable flag. Used for stack discipline and validation in WebAssembly IR processing.
requirements: expr must be a valid wabt::Expr belonging to the currently analyzed function or block context.
A current function context is likely required (BeginFunc should have been called); exact enforcement is implementation-defined.
Unreachable handling behavior is conveyed via the returned Arities.unreachable flag.

functions.name: wabt::LocalTypes::const_iterator::operator++

requirements: The iterator must not be equal to end() when incremented; incrementing a past-the-end iterator results in undefined behavior.

functions.name: wabt::LexerSourceLineFinder::LexerSourceLineFinder
functions.description: Constructor that creates a LexerSourceLineFinder bound to a given LexerSource. Ownership of the provided LexerSource is transferred to the finder, which then allows querying source lines and their byte/column offsets. Usage: construct once with a source, then call GetSourceLine or GetLineOffsets to retrieve data.
requirements: Caller must pass a std::unique_ptr<wabt::LexerSource> by value; ownership is transferred to the constructed object (the unique_ptr will be moved).
After passing the unique_ptr, the caller must not use the original unique_ptr (standard move semantics).
Whether a null source is permitted is unknown (not specified in the header). If null is passed, behavior is unknown.

functions.name: wabt::LexerSourceLineFinder::GetSourceLine
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::LexerSourceLineFinder::GetSourceLine(const wabt::Location& loc, wabt::Offset max_line_length, wabt::LexerSourceLineFinder::SourceLine* out_source_line)
functions.description: Retrieves the text of the source line containing loc and writes it to out_source_line, possibly clamped to max_line_length, along with a column_offset indicating the start column of the returned substring. Returns a Result indicating success or failure. Typical use: after constructing the finder, call with a valid Location to obtain the corresponding line snippet for diagnostics or error reporting.
requirements: out_source_line must be a non-null pointer to receive the result.
max_line_length should be non-negative; semantics for zero or very small values are not specified (unknown).
loc must refer to a location within the associated source; exact valid range and whether lines are 0-based or 1-based are unknown.
Caller must check the returned wabt::Result and handle failure cases appropriately (e.g., when the location is out of range or the line cannot be read).

The SourceLine::line string returned may be truncated to at most max_line_length characters (inferred from parameter naming); exact clamping behavior and how column_offset is computed when clamped are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: wabt::LexerSourceLineFinder::GetLineOffsets
functions.description: Returns the byte offset range corresponding to the specified source line index. Useful for mapping a line number to its [begin, end) offsets within the underlying source buffer. The function reports success or failure via its Result return value.
requirements: out_offsets must be a non-null pointer to receive the offset range.
The acceptable range for line and whether it is 0-based or 1-based are not specified (unknown); caller should use the same convention as Location used with this class.
Caller must check the returned wabt::Result and handle failure cases appropriately (e.g., when the line index is out of bounds or the source cannot be read).

functions.name: wabt::LexerSource::LexerSource
functions.description: Constructs a LexerSource that provides read/seek access over an existing memory buffer. The buffer is not owned by the LexerSource (based on the raw const void*), so the caller is responsible for its lifetime. Typical use is to back a lexer with a contiguous block of bytes and then read from it using Fill/ReadRange/Seek.
requirements: data must point to a contiguous memory region of at least size bytes and remain valid for the entire lifetime of the LexerSource instance
size must correctly describe the number of bytes accessible at data (non-negative and representable in Offset)
The initial read position is at the start of the buffer (inferred from presence of read_offset_)

functions.name: wabt::LexerSource::Clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a new LexerSource that represents the same underlying data as this instance. Intended to provide an independent reader over the same buffer (implementation details not shown).
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized LexerSource instance
The returned unique_ptr owns the cloned LexerSource; the caller assumes ownership and must keep the underlying buffer alive if the clone does not copy it (unknown due to header-only view)
Check the returned pointer before use if allocation can fail (unknown; may return nullptr on allocation failure)

functions.name: wabt::LexerSource::Tell
functions.description: Reports the current read offset within the source buffer via out_offset. Returns a Result status indicating success or failure.
requirements: out_offset must be a non-null pointer to writable memory
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result and only use out_offset on success

functions.name: wabt::LexerSource::Fill
functions.description: Copies up to size bytes from the current read position into dest, advancing the internal read offset by the number of bytes copied. Returns the number of bytes actually written, which may be less than requested (e.g., if the end of the buffer is reached).
requirements: dest must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes
size specifies the maximum number of bytes to copy; behavior for size==0 is a no-op returning 0 (inferred by convention)
Must be called on a valid, initialized LexerSource instance
Callers must handle short reads (return value may be < size)

functions.name: wabt::LexerSource::ReadRange
functions.description: Reads the specified byte range from the source into out_data. The exact semantics (absolute vs. relative range, inclusivity) are not specified in this header; by convention OffsetRange likely denotes an absolute [start, end) or [start, size) range within the buffer.
requirements: The OffsetRange argument must refer to a valid subrange within the underlying buffer (inferred from name and typical usage)
out_data must be a non-null pointer; the vector it points to must be in a valid state to receive data (it will be resized/assigned)
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result before using out_data
Must be called on a valid, initialized LexerSource instance

functions.name: wabt::LexerSource::Seek
functions.description: Sets the current read position to the specified offset within the buffer. Returns a Result indicating success or failure (e.g., if the offset is out of bounds).
requirements: offset should be within the bounds of the underlying buffer (0 <= offset <= size), otherwise a failure Result may be returned (inferred)
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result
Must be called on a valid, initialized LexerSource instance

functions.name: wabt::LexerSource::data
functions.description: Returns the raw pointer to the start of the underlying buffer. The memory is not owned or managed by the returned pointer.
requirements: The returned pointer is only valid as long as the underlying buffer outlives the LexerSource
No const_cast-based modification through this pointer unless the original buffer is mutable and such use is safe (it is returned as const void*)
Must be called on a valid, initialized LexerSource instance

functions.name: wabt::LexerSource::size
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of the underlying buffer.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized LexerSource instance

functions.name: wabt::ParseHexdigit
functions.description: Parses a single hexadecimal digit character and writes its numeric value (0–15) to out. Returns Result::Ok on success, Result::Error if c is not a valid hex digit. Intended for use by the wast-lexer; only minimal validation is performed.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer.
c should be a valid hexadecimal digit in the ranges '0'-'9', 'a'-'f', or 'A'-'F'; otherwise the function returns Result::Error.
No additional validation beyond checking valid hex digit and range is performed.

functions.name: wabt::ParseInt8
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::ParseInt8(const char* s, const char* end, uint8_t* out, wabt::ParseIntType parse_type);
functions.description: Parses an integer literal from the character range [s, end) into an 8-bit integer. Returns Result::Ok on success, Result::Error on overflow or invalid input per the lexer’s guarantees. parse_type controls whether signed forms are accepted or only unsigned. Only overflow is validated; syntax is assumed to have been pre-validated by the wast-lexer.
requirements: s and end must be valid pointers to the same contiguous character buffer; [s, end) denotes the character range to parse.
s must be less than or equal to end; the range may be empty only if the lexer permits (typically should not be empty).
out must be a valid, non-null pointer.
The literal must match the wast-lexer’s integer patterns; only overflow is checked here.
The parsed value must fit in 8 bits; otherwise the function returns Result::Error.
parse_type determines whether signed prefixes/signs are permitted (UnsignedOnly vs SignedAndUnsigned).

functions.name: wabt::ParseInt16
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::ParseInt16(const char* s, const char* end, uint16_t* out, wabt::ParseIntType parse_type);
functions.description: Parses an integer literal from [s, end) into a 16-bit integer. Returns Result::Ok on success; Result::Error on overflow or invalid character sequence (beyond lexer guarantees).
requirements: s and end must delimit a valid contiguous character range; s <= end.
out must be a valid, non-null pointer.
The literal should conform to wast-lexer integer patterns; only overflow is validated here.
Parsed value must fit in 16 bits; otherwise Result::Error is returned.
parse_type controls whether signed and/or unsigned forms are accepted.

functions.name: wabt::ParseInt32
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::ParseInt32(const char* s, const char* end, uint32_t* out, wabt::ParseIntType parse_type);
functions.description: Parses an integer literal from [s, end) into a 32-bit integer. Returns Result::Ok on success; Result::Error on overflow or disallowed format (beyond lexer checks).
requirements: s and end must delimit a valid contiguous character range; s <= end.
out must be a valid, non-null pointer.
The literal should match wast-lexer integer patterns; only overflow is validated here.
Parsed value must fit in 32 bits; otherwise Result::Error is returned.
parse_type controls whether signed and/or unsigned forms are accepted.
