functions.name: wabt::Token::opcode
functions.description: Returns the token's opcode payload. Asserts if the token does not carry an opcode (i.e., HasOpcode() is false).
requirements: Caller must ensure HasOpcode() is true before calling, or an assertion will fail.

functions.name: wabt::Token::literal
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the token's literal payload. Asserts if the token does not carry a literal (i.e., HasLiteral() is false).
requirements: Caller must ensure HasLiteral() is true before calling, or an assertion will fail.
The returned reference remains valid as long as the Token object remains alive.

functions.name: wabt::Token::to_string
functions.description: Formats the token into a human-readable string representation. Useful for logging and diagnostics. Exact format is not specified here.
requirements: No explicit preconditions beyond having a valid Token; note that if implementation inspects payload it may assume the token_type matches the stored payload.

functions.name: wabt::Token::to_string_clamp
functions.description: Formats the token into a string, clamping/truncating the output to at most max_length characters.
requirements: max_length specifies the maximum length of the returned string; no minimum is specified.

functions.name: wabt::TraceScope::TraceScope
functions.description: Deleted default constructor. Prevents creating a TraceScope without specifying a method name (and optionally a formatted message).
requirements: This overload is deleted and cannot be called/instantiated.

functions.name: wabt::TraceScope::~TraceScope
functions.description: Destructor that automatically logs the corresponding exit message for the scope. Intended to be invoked implicitly when the TraceScope object goes out of scope.
requirements: Available only when WABT_TRACING is nonzero at inclusion/compile time; the type is not defined otherwise.
The method string provided at construction must still be valid when the destructor runs (it is referenced to produce the exit message).
Emits to stderr; callers should not assume different output destination.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::type_stack_size
functions.description: Returns the current number of types on the internal evaluation type stack maintained by the TypeChecker while validating instructions. Typical usage: query before/after visiting instructions for debugging or validation.
requirements: The TypeChecker instance must be initialized.
No side effects; can be called at any time.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::IsUnreachable
functions.description: Checks whether the current point in the control flow is unreachable according to the validator’s state (e.g., after an unreachable instruction). Returns a wabt::Result status indicating success/failure of the query and likely encodes the answer via internal state (details not documented).
requirements: Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.
Intended to be called during validation; exact preconditions are unknown.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::GetLabel
functions.description: Retrieves a control-flow label at the given depth from the label stack (0 = innermost). Useful for branch validation and to inspect the target signature.
requirements: out_label must be a non-null pointer to receive the result.
depth must refer to an existing label on the label stack (0 for innermost).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::GetRethrowLabel
functions.description: Retrieves the label suitable for a rethrow operation at the given depth. Intended for exception-handling validation.
requirements: out_label must be non-null.
depth must be within the current label stack and reference a valid EH context (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::GetCatchCount
functions.description: Obtains catch-related information for the label at the given depth. Exact semantics are not documented; likely returns the number of catches or a catch depth (inferred).
requirements: out_depth must be non-null.
depth must be within the current label stack.
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::BeginFunction
functions.description: Begins validation of a function body with the given function signature (params/results). Initializes internal state for type checking of that function.
requirements: sig must contain the function’s parameter and result types; it must be initialized.
Must be called before validating any instructions in a function body (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnAtomicFence
functions.description: Validates an atomic.fence instruction with the provided consistency model operand.
requirements: consistency_model must be an initialized 32-bit value; accepted values are not documented here.
Feature for atomics must be enabled in the TypeChecker’s Features (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnAtomicLoad
functions.description: Validates an atomic load instruction for the given opcode and memory limits (alignment/offset, etc.).
requirements: limits must be initialized and correspond to the targeted memory.
Opcode must be a valid atomic load opcode (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnAtomicNotify
functions.description: Validates an atomic notify instruction with the given opcode and memory limits.
requirements: limits must be initialized and valid for the referenced memory.
Opcode must be a valid atomic notify opcode (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnAtomicStore
functions.description: Validates an atomic store instruction for the given opcode and limits.
requirements: limits must be initialized and valid.
Opcode must be a valid atomic store opcode (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnAtomicRmw
functions.description: Validates an atomic read-modify-write instruction for the given opcode and limits.
requirements: limits must be initialized and valid.
Opcode must be a valid atomic RMW opcode (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnAtomicRmwCmpxchg
functions.description: Validates an atomic compare-exchange instruction for the given opcode and limits.
requirements: limits must be initialized and valid.
Opcode must be a valid cmpxchg opcode (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnAtomicWait
functions.description: Validates an atomic wait instruction for the given opcode and limits.
requirements: limits must be initialized and valid.
Opcode must be a valid atomic wait opcode (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnBinary
functions.description: Validates a binary numeric or reference instruction represented by the opcode (e.g., add, sub, and, or).
requirements: opcode must be a valid binary opcode for the current features (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnBlock
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::TypeChecker::OnBlock(const wabt::TypeVector& param_types, const wabt::TypeVector& result_types)
functions.description: Begins validation of a block construct with specified parameter and result types; pushes a corresponding label onto the control stack.
requirements: param_types and result_types must be initialized type vectors.
Must be paired with a matching OnEnd to close the block (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnBr
functions.description: Validates an unconditional branch to the label at the given depth.
requirements: depth must reference an existing label (0 = innermost).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnBrIf
functions.description: Validates a conditional branch to the label at the given depth.
requirements: depth must reference an existing label.
Requires a condition value on the stack as per Wasm rules (inferred).
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnBrOnNonNull
functions.description: Validates a branch-on-non-null reference to the label at the given depth.
requirements: depth must reference an existing label.
Reference types feature must be enabled (inferred).
Callers must check wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnBrOnNull
functions.description: Validates a branch-on-null reference to the label at the given depth.
requirements: depth must reference an existing label.
Reference types feature must be enabled (inferred).
Callers must check wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::BeginBrTable
functions.description: Begins validation of a br_table instruction, initializing internal tracking of the table’s expected signature.
requirements: Must be followed by one or more OnBrTableTarget calls and a final EndBrTable (inferred).
Callers must check wabt::Result for failure.

functions.name: wabt::TypeChecker::OnBrTableTarget

Useful for validating text data before parsing or display. Specific validation rules beyond standard UTF-8 are not documented here.
requirements: s must point to a contiguous memory region containing at least length readable bytes.
s must not be null when length > 0; when length == 0, s may be null (inferred from pointer/length API).
The function does not modify the buffer (s is const); the memory only needs to be readable.
Provide the exact number of bytes to validate; do not rely on a terminating null character unless it is part of the data.
Callers should check the boolean return value to determine validity of the input UTF-8.

functions.name: wabt::ValidateScript
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::ValidateScript(const wabt::Script* script, wabt::Errors* errors, const wabt::ValidateOptions& options)
functions.description: Validate an entire WebAssembly script (typically a sequence of modules and commands). Performs all validator checks; the script is considered valid if and only if this function returns a success Result. On failure, diagnostics are reported through the provided Errors sink. Intended for use after constructing/parsing a Script AST and before execution or further processing. The function does not mutate the input Script (pointer is const).
requirements: script must be a valid, fully constructed wabt::Script instance; null is not supported (inferred from pointer usage and purpose).
errors must be a valid, non-null wabt::Errors pointer ready to receive diagnostics; caller retains ownership (inferred from output parameter pattern).
options must reference an initialized wabt::ValidateOptions instance controlling feature flags and validation behavior (inferred from type and name).
Callers should check the returned wabt::Result and, on failure, consult errors for details (inferred from comment and return type).

functions.name: wabt::ValidateModule
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::ValidateModule(const wabt::Module* module, wabt::Errors* errors, const wabt::ValidateOptions& options)
functions.description: Validate a single WebAssembly module according to the supplied validation options and enabled features. Returns success if the module passes all validator checks; otherwise returns failure and reports diagnostics via errors. Use after constructing/parsing a Module AST. The function does not modify the input Module (pointer is const).
requirements: module must be a valid, fully constructed wabt::Module instance; null is not supported (inferred from pointer usage and purpose).
errors must be a valid, non-null wabt::Errors pointer to collect diagnostics; caller retains ownership (inferred from output parameter pattern).
options must reference an initialized wabt::ValidateOptions specifying feature flags/behavior (inferred from type and name).
Callers should check the returned wabt::Result and, on failure, consult errors for details (inferred from return type and purpose).

functions.name: wabt::WastLexer::WastLexer
functions.description: Constructs a WebAssembly text (WAT/WAST) lexer over a given LexerSource, associating it with a filename for diagnostics and an optional error collector. Use this to create a lexer instance that will later produce tokens via GetToken(). Notes: the filename is copied internally; the error sink pointer is stored for use during lexing.
requirements: source must point to a valid wabt::LexerSource instance; ownership transfers to the lexer (unique_ptr is consumed).
filename can be any viewable string; it is copied internally so it does not need to outlive the constructor call.
errors may be nullptr (unknown if allowed by implementation); if non-null, the Errors object must remain valid for the lifetime of the WastLexer, since the pointer is stored internally.

The constructed WastLexer instance must be used from the thread/context that manages its underlying source unless external synchronization is provided (thread-safety not documented; treat as non-thread-safe).

functions.name: wabt::WastLexer::CreateBufferLexer
functions.signature: static std::unique_ptr<wabt::WastLexer> wabt::WastLexer::CreateBufferLexer(std::string_view filename, const void* data, size_t size, wabt::Errors* errors)
functions.description: Convenience factory to create a WastLexer that reads from a raw memory buffer. Intended for lexing in-memory WAT/WAST text without creating a custom LexerSource. Returns a newly created lexer instance wrapped in a unique_ptr, or possibly nullptr on failure (behavior not documented).
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory representing the input text to lex.
If size is greater than 0, data should not be null; if size is 0, data may be null (exact allowance not documented).
filename is copied internally and may be used for diagnostics; no lifetime requirements on the input view.
errors may be nullptr (unknown if allowed by implementation); if non-null, the Errors object must remain valid for the lifetime of the returned WastLexer.

The caller assumes ownership of the returned unique_ptr and must maintain the lifetime of input data as required by the created underlying buffer source (not explicitly documented; if the source does not copy data, the buffer must remain valid during lexing).

functions.name: wabt::WastLexer::GetToken
functions.description: Lexes and returns the next token from the input stream. Typical usage is to call repeatedly until an end-of-file token or error is encountered. The token content and location are derived from the internal source and filename provided at construction.
requirements: Must be called on a validly constructed WastLexer instance.
Subsequent calls advance the lexer's internal cursor; tokens are produced in sequence until input is exhausted.
Returned Token should be inspected by the caller to detect EOF or errors as per wabt::Token semantics (exact EOF/error signaling not detailed here).
Do not modify or free the underlying source while iterating; the lexer holds internal pointers/cursors into its source.

functions.name: wabt::WastLexer::MakeLineFinder
functions.description: Creates and returns a helper that can map locations in the lexed source to their corresponding source lines. Useful for diagnostics and error reporting. Internally clones the lexer's source to build the line finder.
requirements: Must be called on a validly constructed WastLexer instance.
The returned unique_ptr transfers ownership to the caller; it should be kept alive as long as line lookup functionality is needed.
Relies on the underlying LexerSource being cloneable; if cloning is unsupported, creation may fail at runtime (behavior not documented).

functions.name: wabt::WastParser::WastParser
functions.description: Constructs a WastParser that reads tokens from the given lexer, reports diagnostics to the provided Errors collection, and uses the specified parse options/features. Intended to be used to parse a single WAT/WAST module or script via the member parsing functions.
requirements: lexer must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized wabt::WastLexer that will outlive the WastParser instance.
errors must be a valid, non-null pointer to a wabt::Errors sink that will outlive the WastParser instance.
options must be a valid, non-null pointer to a wabt::WastParseOptions that will outlive the WastParser instance.
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of lexer, errors, and options; WastParser does not take ownership.

functions.name: wabt::WastParser::Error
functions.description: Reports a formatted error at the given source Location through the parser's Errors sink. Uses printf-style formatting as indicated by the WABT_PRINTF_FORMAT attribute. Typically used internally during parsing to record diagnostics.
requirements: format must be a non-null, printf-style format string compatible with the provided variadic arguments.
The Location should refer to a valid position in the current input; if unknown, a best-effort Location may be passed.
Callers should not assume this throws or aborts; it records an error. Subsequent parse functions may return wabt::Result::Error.

functions.name: wabt::WastParser::ParseModule
functions.description: Parses a single WebAssembly text (WAT) module from the current token stream and returns a Result indicating success or failure. On success, writes a newly constructed Module to out_module.
requirements: out_module must be a non-null pointer to a std::unique_ptr<wabt::Module> storage location.
On successful return (Result::Ok), *out_module is assigned ownership of the parsed Module.
On failure (Result::Error), *out_module may be left unchanged or reset; callers must check the returned Result before using *out_module.
The WastParser must be positioned at the start of a module definition in the token stream.
Parsing behavior is affected by WastParseOptions (e.g., features, parse_binary_modules).

functions.name: wabt::WastParser::ParseScript
functions.description: Parses an entire WAST script (a sequence of commands/modules/actions) from the current token stream. On success, produces a Script object representing the parsed script.
requirements: out_script must be a non-null pointer to a std::unique_ptr<wabt::Script> storage location.
On successful return (Result::Ok), *out_script receives ownership of the parsed Script.
On failure (Result::Error), *out_script may be left unchanged or reset; callers must check the returned Result before using *out_script.
The WastParser must be positioned at the beginning of a script in the token stream.
Parsing behavior is influenced by the parser's WastParseOptions and enabled Features.

functions.name: wabt::WastParser::ReleaseScript
functions.description: Releases and returns any Script object currently owned/held by the parser, transferring ownership to the caller. Typically used after a successful ParseScript when the parser retains an internal Script pointer.
requirements: Caller receives ownership of the returned std::unique_ptr<wabt::Script> and is responsible for its lifetime.
May return an empty std::unique_ptr if no script is available; callers should check for null before use.
Intended to be called after parsing a script; exact timing/lifecycle beyond that is not documented in this header.

functions.name: wabt::ParseWatModule
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::ParseWatModule(wabt::WastLexer* lexer, std::unique_ptr<wabt::Module>* out_module, wabt::Errors* errors, wabt::WastParseOptions* options)
functions.description: Convenience free function that parses a single WAT module from the provided lexer using the given options, reporting diagnostics to errors. On success, returns Result::Ok and stores the parsed Module in out_module.
requirements: lexer must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized wabt::WastLexer providing the input tokens.
out_module must be a non-null pointer to a std::unique_ptr<wabt::Module> storage location; on success it receives ownership of the parsed Module.
errors must be a valid, non-null pointer to a wabt::Errors collector for diagnostics.
options must be a valid, non-null pointer to a wabt::WastParseOptions that configures features and behavior.
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result before using *out_module.

functions.name: wabt::ParseWastScript
functions.signature: wabt::Result wabt::ParseWastScript(wabt::WastLexer* lexer, std::unique_ptr<wabt::Script>* out_script, wabt::Errors* errors, wabt::WastParseOptions* options)
functions.description: Convenience free function that parses a WAST script from the provided lexer using the given options, reporting diagnostics to errors. On success, returns Result::Ok and stores the parsed Script in out_script.
requirements: lexer must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized wabt::WastLexer providing the input tokens.
out_script must be a non-null pointer to a std::unique_ptr<wabt::Script> storage location; on success it receives ownership of the parsed Script.
errors must be a valid, non-null pointer to a wabt::Errors collector for diagnostics.
options must be a valid, non-null pointer to a wabt::WastParseOptions that configures features and behavior.
Callers must check the returned wabt::Result before using *out_script.

functions.name: wabt::WriteWat
functions.signature: wabt::Result WriteWat(wabt::Stream* stream, const wabt::Module* module, const wabt::WriteWatOptions& options)
functions.description: Serializes a WebAssembly Module to its text (WAT) representation and writes it to the provided Stream. Typical usage is to pass a valid wabt::Module you want to pretty-print/dump and a writable wabt::Stream (e.g., file or memory stream). Emission behavior is controlled by WriteWatOptions: features selects the enabled instruction/feature set; fold_exprs toggles folded expression style; inline_export and inline_import control inlining of export/import syntax. Returns a Result indicating success or failure. Details of Result values are defined by the WABT library; ownership of arguments is not transferred.
requirements: stream must be a non-null pointer to a valid, writable wabt::Stream that remains alive for the duration of the call.
module must be a non-null pointer to a well-formed wabt::Module; it must remain valid for the duration of the call.
options must refer to a valid WriteWatOptions object that remains alive for the duration of the call; its fields configure emission (features, fold_exprs, inline_export, inline_import).
Callers should check the returned wabt::Result and handle failure according to WABT’s Result semantics.
The function does not allocate or assume ownership of stream or module; callers are responsible for their lifetime management.

functions.name: wabt::interp::ReadBinaryInterp
functions.signature: wabt::interp::Result wabt::interp::ReadBinaryInterp(std::string_view filename, const void* data, size_t size, const wabt::ReadBinaryOptions& options, wabt::Errors*, wabt::interp::ModuleDesc* out_module)
functions.description: Parses a WebAssembly binary module from the provided memory buffer and produces an interpreter-friendly ModuleDesc. The filename is used for diagnostics. Parsing behavior is controlled by ReadBinaryOptions, and any diagnostics may be reported via the Errors pointer if supplied. Returns a Result indicating success or failure. Typical usage: supply the raw WASM bytes and size, an options struct, an optional Errors sink, and a non-null out_module to receive the decoded module description.
requirements: filename must reference a valid string (std::string_view) that remains valid for the duration of the call.
data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory for the duration of the call.
size is the length in bytes of the WebAssembly binary located at data; it should accurately reflect the buffer size.
options must reference a valid, initialized wabt::ReadBinaryOptions object.
out_module must be a non-null pointer to a wabt::interp::ModuleDesc that can be written to by this function.
Caller must check the returned wabt::interp::Result to determine success or failure.
Behavior for a null wabt::Errors* is unknown from this header; if non-null, it is expected to be a valid pointer to collect diagnostics.

functions.name: wabt::interp::IsNaN
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename std::enable_if<!std::is_floating_point<T>::value, int>::type = 0>
bool WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::IsNaN(T val)
functions.description: Non-floating-point overload. Returns false for any non-floating-point T. Intended as a type-safe IsNaN gate for integral and other non-floating types.
requirements: T must not be a floating-point type (enforced by enable_if).
No other preconditions; always returns false.

functions.name: wabt::interp::CanonNaN

functions.name: wabt::interp::ShiftMask
functions.description: Returns val masked to the low (sizeof(T)*8 - 1) bits. Used to normalize shift counts for rotate/shift operations.

T WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::IntNeg(T val)
functions.description: Two's-complement negation computed as ~val + 1 (wraps on unsigned types).
requirements: T must support bitwise ~ and addition.
For signed T, behavior follows two's-complement wraparound intent; beware of potential signed overflow rules in C++.

T WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::Add(T lhs, T rhs)

If T is floating-point, NaN results may be canonicalized.

functions.description: Returns lhs - rhs, canonicalizing NaN for floating types. For non-floats, CanonNaN is a no-op.

If T is floating-point, NaN results may be canonicalized.

T WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::IntAnd(T lhs, T rhs)

functions.name: wabt::interp::IsNormalDivRem

bool wabt::interp::IsNormalDivRem(T lhs, T rhs)
functions.description: Signed overload. Returns false only for the overflow case (min(T) / -1), true otherwise. Used to distinguish trapping division/remainder cases per WebAssembly semantics on x86.
requirements: T must be a signed integral type (enforced by enable_if).

functions.name: wabt::interp::IntDiv
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
wabt::interp::RunResult WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::IntDiv(T lhs, T rhs, T* out, std::string* out_msg)

requirements: out must be non-null and writable.
out_msg must be non-null and writable.

For signed T, dividing min(T) by -1 traps.

functions.name: wabt::interp::IntRem

requirements: out must be non-null and writable.
out_msg must be non-null and writable.
Callers must check return value; Trap only on divide-by-zero.
Signed min/-1 case yields 0 remainder (not a trap).

functions.name: wabt::interp::FloatAbs

functions.name: wabt::interp::CanConvert
functions.signature:
template <typename R, typename T>
bool WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::CanConvert(T val)
functions.description: Predicate indicating whether val can be converted to R without trapping per WebAssembly numeric conversion rules. Generic template returns true; specializations exist for integer R and float T combinations with precise range checks.
requirements: For specialized overloads, T must be f32 or f64 and R one of s32,u32,s64,u64 (as provided).
Generic template imposes no constraints.

functions.name: wabt::interp::Convert
functions.signature:
template <typename R, typename T>
R WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::Convert(T val)
functions.description: Converts val to type R, asserting CanConvert<R,T>(val). For some cases specializations handle WebAssembly edge cases (e.g., f64->f32 rounding to max finite instead of inf; 64-bit int to float/double via helper functions).
requirements: Callers must ensure CanConvert<R,T>(val) is true; otherwise the assert may fire in debug builds.
R and T must be types supported by static_cast or by provided specializations.
Specialized behavior exists for: R=f32 with T=f64; R=f32/f64 with T=u64/s64 using wabt_convert_* helpers.

functions.name: wabt::interp::IntExtend
functions.signature:
template <typename T, int N>
T WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::IntExtend(T val)
functions.description: Sign-extends the low N+1 bits of val to the full width of T using Hacker’s Delight 2.6 method.
requirements: T must be an integral type supporting shifts, bitwise ops, and subtraction.
N must be in the range [0, (sizeof(T)*8 - 1)].
Left-shifting into the sign bit of a signed T is undefined in C++; to avoid UB, prefer unsigned T or ensure N < sizeof(T)*8 - 1 for signed T.

functions.name: wabt::interp::IntTruncSat
functions.signature:
template <typename R, typename T>
R WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::IntTruncSat(T val)
functions.description: Saturating integer conversion from floating T to integer R. Returns 0 if val is NaN; clamps to [min(R), max(R)] if out-of-range; otherwise returns static_cast<R>(val).
requirements: T must be a floating type accepted by std::isnan and std::signbit.
R must be an integer type with std::numeric_limits bounds.
Behavior depends on CanConvert<R>(val); out-of-range saturates.

functions.name: wabt::interp::Saturate
functions.signature:
template <typename R, typename T>
R WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::Saturate(T val)
functions.description: Clamps val to the representable range of R, where sizeof(R) < sizeof(T).
requirements: sizeof(R) must be less than sizeof(T) (enforced by static_assert).
T must be orderable and convertible to compare against std::numeric_limits<R>::min()/max().

functions.name: wabt::interp::IntAddSat
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U = typename SatPromote<T>::type>
T WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::IntAddSat(T lhs, T rhs)
functions.description: Saturating add: adds lhs and rhs in a wider intermediate type U and clamps the result to T’s range.
requirements: Implicit U defaults via SatPromote<T>; provided only for T in {s8, s16, u8, u16}.
For other T values, SatPromote<T> is undefined; do not instantiate without providing U.
T must be an 8- or 16-bit integer type as specialized.

functions.name: wabt::interp::IntSubSat
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U = typename SatPromote<T>::type>
T WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::IntSubSat(T lhs, T rhs)
functions.description: Saturating subtract: subtracts rhs from lhs in a wider intermediate type U and clamps the result to T’s range.
requirements: Implicit U defaults via SatPromote<T>; provided only for T in {s8, s16, u8, u16}.
For other T values, SatPromote<T> is undefined; do not instantiate without providing U.
T must be an 8- or 16-bit integer type as specialized.

functions.name: wabt::interp::SaturatingRoundingQMul
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T WABT_VECTORCALL wabt::interp::SaturatingRoundingQMul(T lhs, T rhs)
functions.description: Saturating, rounding, "Q" (fixed-point-like) multiply: computes (lhs*rhs + 0.5 ulp) >> (bitwidth-1) and saturates to T’s range. Intended for fixed-point 1.(bitwidth-1) representation.
requirements: T must be an integer type where sizeof(T)*8 <= 32 to avoid overflow in lhs*rhs before widening to int64_t (since the product is computed in T then assigned to int64_t).
For 32-bit T, behavior is defined as intended; for wider T (e.g., 64-bit), lhs*rhs may overflow before being stored in int64_t.

functions.name: wabt::interp::Istream::EmitFixupU32

requirements: Caller must later resolve the placeholder using ResolveFixupU32; exact patching semantics are not documented here
Do not reuse the returned offset for multiple unrelated placeholders
Only call on a valid Istream; behavior with concurrent modifications is undefined

functions.name: wabt::interp::Istream::ResolveFixupU32

requirements: offset must correspond to a fixup placeholder previously returned by EmitFixupU32 on the same Istream
The fixup location must still be valid within the current buffer bounds
Exact value semantics are unknown from the header; consult implementation to supply the correct value

functions.name: wabt::interp::Istream::Trace
functions.signature: wabt::interp::Istream::Offset wabt::interp::Istream::Trace(wabt::Stream* stream, wabt::interp::Istream::Offset from, wabt::interp::Istream::TraceSource* source) const;
functions.description: Executes a tracing pass over the instruction stream starting at the given offset, emitting formatted trace lines to the Stream using callbacks provided by the TraceSource. Returns the next offset after the traced instruction(s).
requirements: stream must be non-null
source must be a valid, non-null TraceSource implementation
from must be within [0, end()) and at an instruction boundary
TraceSource callbacks should be prepared to be called for each instruction read

functions.name: wabt::interp::Istream::TraceSource::~TraceSource
functions.description: Virtual destructor for TraceSource, enabling safe deletion via base pointer.
requirements: If deriving from TraceSource, ensure a virtual destructor is available (provided here) so deleting via base is safe

functions.name: wabt::interp::Istream::TraceSource::Header
functions.description: Pure virtual callback that returns the formatted header string for a trace line given the current stream offset (e.g., stack sizes, offset).
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses
Should return a reasonably short, printable string; exact content is user-defined
May be called frequently; implementation should be efficient

functions.name: wabt::interp::Istream::TraceSource::Pick
functions.description: Pure virtual callback that returns a formatted string to describe an instruction and/or pick information, given an index (e.g., item position) and the decoded instruction.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses
index and instr are provided by the tracer; implementation should not modify them
Should return a printable string describing the instruction or selected fields

functions.name: wabt::interp::Istream::DisassemblySource::Header
functions.description: Default disassembly-header implementation used by Disassemble, producing per-line header text for a given offset.
requirements: offset is the current stream offset for the disassembled instruction
Override exists primarily for internal use; callers normally do not invoke this directly

functions.name: wabt::interp::Istream::DisassemblySource::Pick
functions.description: Default disassembly-line body implementation that formats the given instruction for human-readable output.
requirements: index and instr are inputs from the disassembler; should be treated as read-only

// Exercise for uint16_t (promotion path) and uint32_t (regular path).
uint16_t a16 = (uint16_t)(*FUZZ_PARAM(uint32_t)); uint16_t b16 = (uint16_t)(*FUZZ_PARAM(uint32_t)); uint16_t r16 = wabt::interp::Mul<uint16_t>(a16, b16); uint16_t expect16 = (uint16_t)((uint32_t)a16 * (uint32_t)b16); FUZZ_ASSERT(r16 == expect16, "Mul<u16> must multiply in widened type and truncate to u16"); uint32_t a32 = *FUZZ_PARAM(uint32_t); uint32_t b32 = *FUZZ_PARAM(uint32_t); uint32_t r32 = wabt::interp::Mul<uint32_t>(a32, b32); uint32_t expect32 = (uint32_t)(a32 * b32); FUZZ_ASSERT(r32 == expect32, "Mul<u32> must match builtin * with wrap semantics"); // Validation: both 16-bit promotion and 32-bit cases match expected semantics.

data_types.description: An unconstrained byte string used as a C/C++ string or std::string_view. It may contain any bytes including ASCII or UTF-8; when passed as a C-string it is expected to include no embedded nulls if full content is to be consumed via strlen, but fuzzing may include arbitrary content. Suitable for names, identifiers, or general text parameters.

An arbitrary byte buffer treated as opaque binary data. No encoding or structure is assumed. Used for inputs like file payloads, WebAssembly binaries, or custom section bytes where the consumer interprets bytes directly.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import itertools

# We need to generate interesting, but valid, arbitrary strings to drive many FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# calls across various stubs. The stubs expect:
# - WebAssembly-like binaries for ReadBinary* paths
# - Reasonable identifier/name strings (module/function/local names)
# - Paths/filenames (for diagnostics)
# - Small payload blobs (metadata, custom sections)
# - Format strings will be chosen internally; we just provide data args.
#
# Strategy:
# - Assemble a composite buffer made of multiple concatenated length-prefixed strings so fuzzer runtime can
#   slice them for FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(). The harness typically pulls sequentially.
# - Include a minimal valid WASM binary (magic, version, and a simple custom section) to seed ReadBinaryIr/Interp.
# - Mix in ASCII identifiers, snake/camel case, numbers, and some Unicode where safe, but avoid huge strings.
# - Include some filenames with extensions used by wabt (.wasm, .wat, .wast, .json) and paths with slashes.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Minimal valid WASM: magic + version (1), with an empty custom section to remain valid but simple.
# 00: 0x00 61 73 6d (magic) 01 00 00 00 (version)
# Optionally append a custom section (id=0) with name "x" and empty payload.
# Section encoding: id(0) | size(LEB) | name_len(LEB) | name bytes | payload

def uleb(n):
    # encode unsigned LEB128
    out = bytearray()
    v = n & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    while True:
        b = v & 0x7F
        v >>= 7
        if v:
            out.append(b | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

def minimal_wasm():
    b = bytearray(b"\x00asm\x01\x00\x00\x00")
    # Custom section with name "x" and small data "d"
    name = b"x"
    payload = b"d"
    body = uleb(len(name)) + name + payload
    sec = bytearray()
    sec.append(0)  # id
    sec += uleb(len(body))
    sec += body
    b += sec
    return bytes(b)

def rand_ident(r):
    # Produce identifier-like string [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* with occasional camel/snake
    start = r.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_")
    rest = ''.join(r.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_") for _ in range(r.randint(0, 20)))
    return start + rest

def rand_snake_words(r, n):
    return "_".join(rand_ident(r).lower() for _ in range(n))

def rand_unicode_safe(r, n):
    # sprinkle some safe Latin-1 printable chars
    chars = [chr(r.randint(0x20, 0x7E)) for _ in range(max(0, n-3))]
    # add a couple of extended bytes
    for _ in range(3):
        chars.append(chr(r.randint(0xA1, 0xFF)))
    r.shuffle(chars)
    return ''.join(chars)

def rand_filename(r):
    bases = [rand_ident(r), rand_snake_words(r, r.randint(1,3)), "module", "script", "test"]
    exts = [".wasm", ".wat", ".wast", ".json", ".bin"]
    base = r.choice(bases)
    ext = r.choice(exts)
    # occasional nested path
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        dirs = [rand_ident(r).lower() for _ in range(r.randint(1,3))]
        sep = "/"
        return sep.join(dirs + [base + ext])
    return base + ext

def lp(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # length-prefixed with 16-bit little-endian length (fits our sizes)
    return struct.pack('<H', len(s)) + s

def make_string_pool(r):
    pool = []
    # Names and identifiers
    for _ in range(10):
        pool.append(rand_ident(r).encode('utf-8'))
    for _ in range(6):
        pool.append(rand_snake_words(r, r.randint(1,4)).encode('utf-8'))
    # Filenames
    for _ in range(6):
        pool.append(rand_filename(r).encode('utf-8'))
    # Paths with backslashes to exercise ConvertBackslashToSlash
    for _ in range(3):
        parts = [rand_ident(r) for __ in range(r.randint(2,4))]
        pool.append("\\".join(parts).encode('utf-8'))
    # Small payloads / metadata
    for _ in range(6):
        n = r.randint(1, 64)
        pool.append(rand_unicode_safe(r, n).encode('latin1', errors='ignore'))
    # A couple of empty or single-char strings avoided; ensure non-empty as many stubs require non-empty
    # Include typical section/custom names
    pool += [b"name", b"custom", b"dylink", b"feature", b"comdat", b"meta", b"data", b"func", b"global", b"table", b"tag"]
    # Keep individual lengths modest
    return pool


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    out = bytearray()

    # Start with a minimal valid wasm to seed binary readers.
    wasm = minimal_wasm()
    out += lp(wasm)

    # Add a small JSON-ish snippet for WriteBinarySpecScript stream names
    jsonish = b'{"script":[]}'
    out += lp(jsonish)

    # Add a pool of strings, each length-prefixed, so FUZZ_PARAM_STR slices can be satisfied in sequence
    pool = make_string_pool(r)
    r.shuffle(pool)
    for s in pool:
        # cap overly long strings
        if len(s) > 256:
            s = s[:256]
        out += lp(s)

    # Add several filenames explicitly
    for _ in range(5):
        fn = rand_filename(r).encode('utf-8')
        out += lp(fn)

    # Add some numeric blobs for leb128 paths
    for _ in range(8):
        # 32-bit and 64-bit little endian values embedded as strings (binary blobs)
        v32 = r.getrandbits(32)
        v64 = r.getrandbits(64)
        blob = struct.pack('<IQ', v32, v64)
        out += lp(blob)

    # Ensure total size cap
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])
